record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.original_question: In mapping theory, can every locally invertible mapping of interest, including a quasi-isometric mapping, be approximated by a sequence of locally invertible piecewise-affine mappings that converges to it? Here quasi-isometric means that local metric distortion is uniformly controlled, for example by bounded singular values or by a condition of the form det grad y > t Phi(det grad y, grad y).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain and let $y:\Omega 	o \mathbb{R}^n$ be a locally invertible mapping (i.e., every point of $\Omega$ has a neighborhood on which $y$ is a homeomorphism onto its image). Call $y$ quasi-isometric if its local metric distortion is uniformly controlled — for example, if $y$ is differentiable a.e. and the singular values of $
abla y(x)$ are bounded above and below by positive constants uniformly in $x$, or equivalently if there exist $t>0$ and a suitable continuous function $\Phi$ such that
$$\det 
abla y(x) \;>\; t\,\Phi igl(\det 
abla y(x),\,
abla y(x) igr) \qquad 	ext{for a.e. } x\in\Omega.$$
Question: does there exist a sequence $\{y_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ of locally invertible piecewise-affine mappings $y_k:\Omega	o\mathbb{R}^n$ (each affine on the cells of some simplicial subdivision of $\Omega$) such that $y_k 	o y$ in an appropriate function-space topology (e.g.\ uniform convergence together with convergence of gradients in $L^p$)? More generally, can every locally invertible mapping of interest be approximated by locally invertible piecewise-affine mappings in this sense?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of approximating homeomorphisms (and quasi-isometric / Sobolev locally invertible maps) by piecewise-affine homeomorphisms is classical and has been resolved in the planar case (results of Iwaniec–Kovalev–Onninen, Hencl–Pratelli and others), but in dimensions n ≥ 3 the analogous approximation question remains largely open. Recent work (e.g. on diffeomorphic approximation of piecewise affine homeomorphisms, 2025) explicitly states that the higher-dimensional approximation of Sobolev homeomorphisms by piecewise-affine homeomorphisms or diffeomorphisms is open in dimensions 3 and 4, with only partial progress.
